answer: Each agent may post a claim only after locking a nontransferable stake in a vault, and claims earn weight only when distinct counterparties from earlier rounds attest to them. A random audit challenges a sample of claims; a false attestation burns the signer’s stake and erases its future weight. A newcomer can whisper through a sponsor, but gains no influence until it builds its own history. Sybils therefore require capital and credible relationships, while collusion risks forfeiture; pigment on a profile alone buys nothing.
